findings.original: whether soot, with which, unknown to the buyer, 90% of dust and sand are mixed, is genuine soot in the commercial sense or adulterated soot in the legal sense
findings.rewrite: is soot that, without the buyer’s knowledge, has 90% of dust and sand mixed into it “genuine” soot in the commercial sense, or adulterated soot in the legal sense?
findings.problem: Scare quotes around "genuine" are added; Marx has none here, and §1.2 treats quotation marks as attribution/irony markers, so none may be invented.
findings.fix: Remove the quotation marks: "... has 90% of dust and sand mixed into it genuine soot in the commercial sense, or adulterated soot in the legal sense?"

findings.original: We have hitherto considered the tendency to the extension of the working day
findings.rewrite: So far we have looked at the drive to lengthen the working day
findings.problem: "Tendency" becomes "drive", which is stronger and more willful than Marx's word.
findings.fix: So far we have looked at the tendency to lengthen the working day

findings.original: it will be understood that the Report of the Commission classes journeymen bakers among the short-lived labourers
findings.rewrite: it will be understood why the Report of the Commission classes journeymen bakers among the short-lived workers
findings.problem: "that" becomes "why", which turns the statement that the report classes bakers this way into a claim about the report's reasons.
findings.fix: it will be understood that the Report of the Commission classes journeymen bakers among the short-lived workers

findings.problem: "Torpor" means stupor or sluggishness of mind and body, which leads into "their brain ceased to think"; "numbness" narrows it to a loss of physical feeling.

findings.original: (carried ready-moulded articles into the drying-room, afterwards bringing back the empty mould)
findings.rewrite: (carried the newly moulded articles into the drying-room, and afterwards brought back the empty mould)
findings.problem: This explanatory parenthesis is outside the quotation marks (only "ran moulds" is quoted), so §1.5 calls for American spelling.
findings.fix: Use "molded" and "mold" in the parenthesis, and keep "ran moulds" inside the quotation marks.

findings.problem: British spelling is left in Marx's own voice.

notes_review: The logged judgment calls are sound. These include: no §7 gloss for 'manufacture' (ordinary sense only), keeping 'sophisticated' for the pun, the literal re-translation of the Carlyle/Schiller line, the 'Ixxi'→'lxxi' and stray-'in' fixes, keeping the singular 'employee', and the 1.03 length ratio justified by near-verbatim testimony (confirmed: p041, p053, p055, p061, p068, p074, p076, p084 and the quotations in nn. 55, 57, 58 match word for word apart from the logged changes). The phthisis→tuberculosis and dyspepsia→indigestion substitutions in Arledge's quotation fall within §2.1 and do not change the medical claim.
summary: Fidelity is high: every number, name, citation, quotation, attribution and ironic tag (the newly imported Princess of Wales, 'abstemious', iterum Crispinus, the Royal 'we') survives, and the only problems are a few small wording shifts and one added pair of scare quotes. Readability meets the target, with long periodic sentences split cleanly, neutral glosses kept short, and §7 explanations given correctly at first use for bourgeois, labor process and proletariat.
